# read_C: pp. 78–79 (leaves n79–n80), established from the images

Line counts:
- p. 78 has five lines. It is a leaf back, so it has no ornament (checked). The margin is described below.
- p. 79 has **three** lines. It is a leaf front and opens with ༄༅༔ ༔: the ornament, its ༔, a wide blank, and a second ༔ before འོད. Below line 3 the frame is empty.

That makes 8 print lines. The witness's line breaks match the print on all 8.

**End of the part and of text kha.** 79.3 ends …ཐོས་གྲོལ་ཆེན་མོ་ཐལ་ལོ༔ ཨྠྀི༔ རྒྱ་རྒྱ་རྒྱ༔ ༔. There are wide blanks before the mantric stack and before རྒྱ, and a last, faint ༔ stands against the inner right frame rule (see below). Nothing follows, so the part ends at the end of p. 79.

Method:
- Line bands were found from the row profile. Headlines are at about n79 y≈125/180/235/290/345 and n80 y≈140/200/255.
- Each line was cropped at ×4 (LANCZOS) in six overlapping segments.
- Doubtful syllables were cropped at ×6 to ×10, and pixel dumps (threshold 128 or 150) were made for tshegs and for the margin mark.

## The mantric syllable (79.3)

At ×8 the print shows **one stack**: ཨ over a subjoined **ཐ (ྠ)**, with a **double gi-gu** above it. I transcribe it ཨྠྀི, keeping the witness's vowel order and correcting its ྛ.

- **The upper letter.** It is ཨ: a full-height stem on the right, and on the left a short bent stroke enclosing a curl.
- **The lower letter.** It hangs from the same right-hand stem, and its two loops lie on the **left** of the stem. That is the shape of ཐ. Retroflex ཋ (ྛ) is the mirror image, with the stem on the left. So it is ཐ, not ཋ.
- **The vowel.** It is two gi-gu curls joined back to back, a "∞" with one tail sweeping down-left and one down-right. That is a reversed gi-gu (ྀ) plus a normal gi-gu (ི).

This is the treasure-text closing **ཨི་ཐི** (iti, "thus") written as one ligature, with one i-vowel for each letter. It is followed by ༔, a wide blank, and རྒྱ་རྒྱ་རྒྱ༔ (tsheg dots visible between the three རྒྱ).

No fix is proposed. It stays as printed.

## Margins

- **n79 (p. 78), left margin:** Arabic **78**, printed sideways, near the top. This is the reproduction's page number. There is no Tibetan.
- **n80 (p. 79), left margin:** Arabic **79** and **80**, sideways. Below them is a short Tibetan marginal label. It reads as **སོ་དྲུག** ("36"), followed by one stack I could not read with confidence. 36 is the right leaf number for text kha: p. 9 is its leaf 1 front, and (79 − 9) / 2 + 1 = 36. So it is the folio mark, not text.
- **n80, right end of line 3:** a faint mark at x 1863–1878, y 284–320, inside the inner frame rule. Where it lies, the rule is broken. In the pixel dump it is a ring, a short bar, and the remains of a lower ring: a ༔ printed faint. It is the witness's final " ༔", kept. A close call, but the shape is clear in the dump.

Close calls not marked [?]:
- **79.2 (line end) བར་.** No separate blob. But the head bar of ར runs about 6 px past where a mid-line ར head ends (×10, against 79.2 གྲོལ་བར་ངེས), and finishes in a raised knob. I read that as a tsheg fused to the bar, as at 60.5 in part 006. The witness has the tsheg. If the drafter reads none, the fix is `# fix: འཆི་ཁའི་བརདོ་ལ => འཆི་ཁའི་བར་དོ་ལ`.
- **78.2 ཀྱཻ (double vowel).** At ×10 there are two parallel strokes. The left one touches a stem coming down from line 1, but it bends diagonally where the stem would run straight, so it is a vowel stroke. Witness confirmed. The print uses ཀྱཻ elsewhere, e.g. 61.2.
- **78.3 ཚེ.** Above ཚ, after the gi-gu of འི, stand a thin "\" stroke and a thicker hooked blob. I read them as one e-vowel plus ink: ཚཻ is not a reading. Witness ཚེ kept.

## Witness readings checked and confirmed though odd

- 78.1 **ཁོན་ནས** (×8): ཁ with na-ro, then ན, a tsheg dot, then ནས. There is no tsheg between ཁོ and ན. The other recension has ཁོ་ནར. See misprints.
- 78.1 དྲང་དུ (also 78.2 ལམ་སྣ་དྲང་དུ). The other recension has དྲངས་དུ.
- 78.1 **སྙམ་པའི་མདུན་བརྩེ་གཅིག་ཏུ** (×8): མ, then ད with zhabs-kyu, then ན. Next comes a closed box, the same triangular interior as the བ of བཟུང, touching the རྩེ stack with no tsheg. Reader B's witness has the same མདུན་བརྩེ་གཅིག at 76/77. Elsewhere the print has འདུན་པ་རྩེ་གཅིག (part 005) and མདུན་པ་རྩེ་གཅིག (part 007). See misprints.
- 78.1 ཞིང་དུ་ད་ལྟ (×5; with zhabs-kyu, then ད).
- 78.2 ཐོབ་ཅིག.
- 78.3 ཚོགས་ཀྱི་ལམ་སྣ (the other recension has རྣམས་ཀྱིས).
- 78.4 **ཀྱང་༔**: a tsheg before ༔ (a separate dot at headline height, ×4). Every other ༔ on these pages has none.
- 79.2 ངན་ཡང (the other recension has ཀྱང).
- 79.3 **ཐལ་ལོ༔**: ཐ, ལ, then ལ with na-ro. The other recension has ལགས་སོ.

Line-end tshegs:
- 78.1 ལམ་, 78.3 སྣ་, 78.4 མཁའ་, 78.5 འཇའ་ and 79.1 རིགས་: a dot is visible after the last letter.

## Suspected misprints

1. **78.1 ཁོན་ནས.** Read as printed: "right now, from there (?)". The expected text is ཁོ་ནར ("this very moment", the other recension's reading). It could also be ཁོ་ན་ནས. The sense allows more than one reading, so it is **kept, note only**. Certainty that something is wrong: moderate.
2. **78.1 མདུན་བརྩེ་གཅིག་ཏུ** for འདུན་པ་རྩེ་གཅིག་ཏུ ("with one-pointed longing"). The print has the same form twice in this part (Reader B's stretch too), so it may be this block's habit. **Kept, note only.**

Not misprints, the print's own spelling: དྲང་དུ (for དྲངས), ཀྱཻ, ཐལ་ལོ.

Seal, seal, seal."); other recension …ཐོས་གྲོལ་ཆེན་མོ་ལགས་སོ༔ ("…is [this]"), with no ithi and no seals, running straight on into ད་ནི་ཁྲོ་བོའི་བར་དོར…**. In this print the wrathful bardo is a separate text (ga), so the peaceful part closes here as a text of its own.

## Proposed name

`# name: Day seven: the knowledge-holders and ḍākinīs, the animal light, the prayer; the peaceful bardo closes`

(My stretch, pp. 78–79, is the end of the day-seven prayer to the knowledge-holders and the colophon of text kha. The name covers pp. 72–79 as briefed.)
